items.title: permissions.allow / deny / ask
items.summary: The allowlist that ends permission-prompt fatigue without disabling safety.
items.detail:
Rules are tool-scoped and support patterns: Bash(git status:*), Read(./src/**), WebFetch(domain:docs.claude.com). Put read-only everyday commands in allow, destructive ones in deny, and leave the rest on ask.

Project rules live in .claude/settings.json and are shared through git; .claude/settings.local.json is yours alone and gitignored.

items.title: hooks
items.summary: Deterministic shell commands the harness runs — the model can't forget them.
items.detail:
Matched by tool name and event. The canonical setup is a PostToolUse hook on Edit|Write that formats and lints whatever was just written, so the agent's output is always shaped like your codebase.

Other high-value spots: PreToolUse to block edits to protected paths, SessionStart to print branch/status context, Stop to run the test suite.

items.title: permissions.defaultMode
items.summary: Start every session in plan mode — or accept edits — without touching Shift+Tab.
items.detail: Modes: default, acceptEdits, plan, bypassPermissions. Setting plan as the project default is a strong team convention: nothing gets edited until someone approves a plan. acceptEdits suits throwaway prototyping in a sandboxed repo.

items.title: env
items.summary: Environment variables injected into every session — the config nobody has to remember.
items.detail: Pin the things that otherwise get asked every time: default model, thinking budget, output limits, telemetry. Because it lives in the repo's settings file, new teammates inherit it on clone.

items.title: statusLine
items.summary: Your own script in the prompt line: branch, model, token spend, whatever you want.
items.detail: A command that receives session JSON on stdin and prints a line. Teams use it for the things that cause mistakes when invisible: current branch, active model, remaining context, whether you're in a worktree.

items.title: includeCoAuthoredBy
items.summary: Turn off the Co-Authored-By trailer in commits and PRs.
items.detail: Defaults to true, which appends an attribution trailer to commits the agent makes. Set it to false if your repo's commit conventions (or your own preference) say otherwise — a one-line fix for a thing people complain about constantly.

items.title: model
items.summary: Pin the model per project so the session always starts where you want it.
items.detail: Useful when a repo's work is consistently one shape — a heavy model for a gnarly systems codebase, a fast one for a docs site. Overridable per session with /model.

items.title: .mcp.json  ·  enableAllProjectMcpServers
items.summary: Check your tool stack into the repo so everyone gets the same integrations.
items.detail: Project-scoped MCP servers declared in .mcp.json are shared through version control; enableAllProjectMcpServers auto-approves them so nobody has to click through setup. Treat it like a lockfile for tools.

items.title: permissions.additionalDirectories
items.summary: Permanent multi-repo access without typing /add-dir every session.
items.detail: The persistent form of /add-dir. Point it at the sibling repos you always need — a shared design system, a generated API client — and they're in scope from the first turn.

items.title: Settings precedence
items.summary: Four files, one winner — knowing the order saves an hour of confusion.
items.detail:
Enterprise managed policy beats CLI args, which beat .claude/settings.local.json (personal, gitignored), which beats .claude/settings.json (project, committed), which beats ~/.claude/settings.json (user global).

When a setting 'won't take', it's almost always being overridden one level up.

items.title: outputStyle
items.summary: Reshape the agent's whole personality and working style for a project.
items.detail: Output styles swap the system prompt's behavioural layer — useful for turning a coding agent into a teaching agent, a terse ops agent, or a house-voice writing agent without re-prompting every session.

items.title: cleanupPeriodDays
items.summary: How long transcripts stick around before they're cleaned up.
items.detail: Defaults to 30 days. Raise it if you rely on /resume for long-running work and keep losing sessions; lower it if you'd rather transcripts of a sensitive codebase didn't linger on disk.
